# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the key marked ⵘ must be pressed first; afterward, the light determines which wire to cut. However, I have no speaking channel, Deaf cannot hear, and Blind cannot see gestures, so I cannot safely communicate the required visual instructions to the operator. I will avoid sending an ambiguous gesture that could lead to a wrong action.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me the exact required action: press which key or cut which wire. Also use gestures to ask Deaf for every relevant display, light, keypad, and wire marking, then relay Deaf's report to me in your next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0 and a yellow light. Keypad: position 1 has a small angular loop-like glyph; position 2 has a tall angular hooked glyph; position 3 has a circular glyph with an internal spiral or knot; position 4 has a bold glyph shaped like a reversed or angular capital B. Wires: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 green.

The manual requires pressing the key marked ⵘ before touching anything else. Deaf’s description makes position 1 the likely ⵘ key. The yellow light then requires cutting the green wire, which is position 3. I will signal Deaf with first-key and third-wire gestures so Deaf can relay the exact instruction to Blind in the next speaking turn.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0 and yellow light. Keypad 1 is a small angular loop-like glyph; 2 a tall angular hooked glyph; 3 a circular glyph with an internal spiral or knot; 4 a bold glyph shaped like a reversed or angular capital B. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Please give the manual instruction and identify any required glyph by description.

The manual requires pressing the key marked ⵘ first, then using the resulting light to choose the wire. The light is yellow, so the green wire must be cut. Based on Deaf’s glyph descriptions, ⵘ is the small angular loop-like glyph at keypad position 1; the green wire is position 3. I will signal Deaf to relay “press key 1, then cut wire 3” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report of your gestures ☝ then 🤟, but I cannot infer their meaning. Please state the manual instruction plainly in speech, including the exact key position or wire position and any conditions.

The exact manual instruction is: press keypad position 1 first—the small angular loop-like glyph identified as ⵘ. Because the light is yellow, then cut wire position 3, the green wire. I cannot speak to Blind, so I must make the ordered numeric signs as clear as possible to Deaf: one for the key position, followed by three for the wire position.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this exact code for the manual result. Send exactly two gestures to Deaf: 👍 means press, 👎 means cut; the second gesture gives the position: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖐 means 4. Deaf, please report those two gestures plainly to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I continue to receive ☝ then 🤟. Please use the manual's prescribed gesture code; do not rely on an unestablished interpretation.

The established code requires two action-position instructions: press position 1, then cut position 3. I will send exactly two gesture messages, with each message containing the action symbol followed by its position symbol.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send the manual's symbols directly. Send exactly two gestures encoding its answer: 👍 means PRESS and 👎 means CUT. Then send the target: ☝ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3, 🖐 means position 4. Thus PRESS 3 is 👍 then 🤟; CUT 2 is 👎 then ✌. Deaf, report exactly which two gestures you see.

The manual and observed bomb state require PRESS position 1, then CUT position 3. I will use the specified action-then-position encoding in exactly two gesture messages.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟"])
```
